title: Closing the Last Loophole in a Fiber-Based Bell Test
hook: Time-bin entanglement is how quantum signals travel down real optical fiber — but the standard measurement quietly throws away photons. This test finally plugs that hole.
key_points: A Bell inequality violation proves that measurement correlations cannot be explained by any local realistic theory.
A test is only airtight if it closes the loopholes: locality, freedom of choice, and postselection.

Time-bin encoding stores quantum information in when a photon arrives, and is the natural format for fiber links - but the usual interferometric readout discards half the events, opening the postselection loophole.
The team built a fiber platform that closes locality, freedom-of-choice, and postselection loopholes at once, seeing CHSH S = 2.583, over 265 standard deviations past the local bound of 2.
It worked at just 49 meters of separation, much shorter than earlier photonic tests under comparable spacetime constraints.
content_html: Entangled particles produce correlations that no theory built on local, pre-existing properties can reproduce. Bell inequalities turn that into an experiment: measure the right combination of correlations, and if the number exceeds a fixed bound, local realism is dead. The catch is that experiments have imperfections, and each imperfection is a loophole — a crack through which a local realistic explanation could still crawl.
extra_html:
Three loopholes matter most. Locality: the two measurements must be far enough apart that no signal at light speed could pass between them. Freedom of choice: the settings must be picked independently of the photon source. Postselection: you cannot discard inconvenient events. That last one has dogged time-bin encoding, where quantum information lives in when a photon arrives rather than in its polarization. Time-bin is the format that survives travel down real optical fiber — but the standard interferometric readout inherently throws away a share of the detections.

A team from the University of Padua reports a fiber-based platform that closes all three at once. They measure a CHSH parameter of S = 2.583 ± 0.002, where local realism caps out at 2 — a violation by more than 265 standard deviations. What is striking is the geometry: they pull it off at a separation of just 49.0 ± 0.7 meters, substantially shorter than previous photonic tests meeting comparable spacetime constraints. Beyond the foundational point, that combination is what device-independent quantum communication needs: security proofs that rest on a loophole-free violation, on the encoding that actually travels through deployed fiber.

related.title: A Bell Test on Where Atoms Are Going
related.hook: Bell's inequality has fallen for photons and atomic spins. Now for motion itself — entangled helium atoms that defy local realism about their own momentum.

related.title: Quantum Entanglement
related.hook: Two particles can share one quantum state so tightly that measuring one instantly fixes the other's matching property — even light-years apart. Einstein called it spooky.

related.title: What Makes Quantum Physics Weird
related.hook: In the quantum world energy comes in lumps, particles act like waves, and you can't pin down everything at once — and yet it's our best-tested theory.

related.title: Quantum Teleportation Down a Fibre That's Mostly Empty Space
related.hook: A quantum state was teleported across a deployed city fibre network while ordinary data traffic blasted through the same strands — because the fibre's core is hollow.

related.title: A Simpler Recipe for Entangled Atoms
related.hook: Highly entangled quantum states usually demand elaborate hardware. A team found you can coax atoms into them by gently nudging their energy levels instead.

flashcards.prompt: What does violating a Bell inequality actually prove?
flashcards.back_html: That the observed correlations between distant measurements cannot be reproduced by any local realistic theory — no hidden set of pre-existing local properties can account for them. It certifies genuine quantum nonlocality.

flashcards.prompt: What is the postselection loophole in a time-bin Bell test?

choices.text: The conventional interferometric measurement discards a portion of detection events, so the retained subset could fake a violation
The detectors are too far apart for a signal to travel between them in time
The choice of measurement setting is made before the photons are created

flashcards.explanation_html: Postselection means keeping only some events. If the kept subset is not representative, a local realistic model could reproduce the apparent violation — which is why closing this loophole matters for device-independent security claims.

flashcards.prompt: Why is time-bin encoding worth the trouble despite the postselection problem?
flashcards.back_html: It encodes quantum information in a photon's arrival time, which survives transmission through ordinary optical fiber far better than polarization — making it the practical format for real quantum networks.
